domain: Subtraction of fractions, mixed numbers, and whole numbers with simplification

skills.name: Prepare operands for subtraction
skills.definition: Rewrite operands into a subtraction-ready form before executing subtraction, including establishing a common denominator for unlike fractions and normalizing whole or mixed-number forms without changing value.
skills.merge_rationale: S01 and S02 are both preparatory transformations applied before subtraction. In the dossiers, both serve the same problem-solving phase: making operands compatible for later subtraction. Although they are not identical operations, they are diagnostically close at a coarser level because both are value-preserving rewrites that enable aligned subtraction.

skills.name: Subtract aligned parts
skills.definition: Carry out subtraction once operands are in compatible form, including subtracting numerators over a common denominator and subtracting whole and fractional parts of mixed numbers.
skills.merge_rationale: Kept separate because execution of subtraction is a distinct cognitive operation from preparation, regrouping, and simplification. It remains a major diagnostic breakpoint across nearly all items.

skills.name: Regroup to complete subtraction
skills.definition: Borrow or regroup across the whole part when the fractional part would otherwise be negative, rewriting one whole as a fraction with the current denominator.
skills.merge_rationale: Kept separate because borrowing/regrouping has a distinctive error pattern and only occurs in a subset of mixed-number or whole-minus-fraction items. It should remain visible diagnostically.

skills.name: Simplify result
skills.definition: Reduce the post-subtraction result to lowest terms or simplify zero-fraction expressions to whole-number results.
skills.merge_rationale: Kept separate because simplification is a finalization skill with different error patterns from subtraction itself. Students may subtract correctly but fail to simplify.
